title: Expressions, like terms and substitution
summary: Build expressions with algebra tiles, collect like terms, cancel zero pairs, then substitute a value for x.
guide: This studio follows KS3 algebra: writing and simplifying expressions by collecting like terms, and substituting numbers into expressions.
The tiles: a big square is {{alg:x^2}}, a long strip is {{alg:x}}, and a small square is {{alg:1}}. A red tile is the negative of the same tile: a red strip is {{alg:-x}}.
An {{term:algebraic-expression}} such as {{alg:2x + 3}} has two {{term:term}}s. In {{alg:2x}}, 2 is the {{term:coefficient}} and x is the {{term:variable}}; 3 is the {{term:constant}}.
{{term:like-terms}} have the same letters with the same powers, so they are the same shape of tile: {{alg:3x}} and {{alg:-x}} are like terms, but {{alg:x}} and {{alg:x^2}} are not.
A white tile and a red tile of the same shape make 0: a zero pair. Tap one, then the other, to take them off. Tiles of different shapes never cancel.
To substitute, flip the tiles: each strip shows the value of x. A red tile means take that amount away. Type your answers on the keypad under the tiles.

engine.label-empty: Tap a tile above to put it here.
engine.label-unlike: {t} and {u} are different shapes, so they are not a zero pair.
engine.instruction-build: Tap tiles to build the expression.
engine.instruction-read: Tap a white and a red tile of the same shape.
engine.instruction-flip: Flip the tiles, then add them up.

build-expression.title: Build 2x + 3
build-expression.prompt: Build {{alg:2x + 3}} on the mat. Which tile is x, and which is 1? Predict how many of each you need, then tap them in the tray.
build-expression.hint: 2x means two x strips. The 3 is three small squares.
build-expression.success: Well done! Two x strips and three small squares: {{alg:2x + 3}}.
build-expression.why: Why can't you write {{alg:2x + 3}} as {{alg:5x}}? Which number is the coefficient and which is the constant?
build-expression.model: Because a strip and a small square are different shapes: x is not 1, so 2 strips and 3 squares cannot be counted as 5 strips. The coefficient 2 tells you how many x strips; the constant 3 is the number on its own, three small squares.

feedback.empty: The mat is empty. Tap tiles in the tray to put them on the mat.
feedback.unlike-added: You made {{alg:5x}}: five strips. But the 3 in {{alg:2x + 3}} is not x: it is three small squares.
feedback.x-plus-x-is-x2: The big square is {{alg:x^2}}, which is x × x. But 2x is x + x: two strips side by side.
feedback.swapped: That is {{alg:3x + 2}}: three strips and two small squares. Look again: the 2 belongs to x.
feedback.no-x: You used only small squares, so this is just 5. Where are the x strips?
feedback.sign: Some of your tiles are red. Red tiles are negative; {{alg:2x + 3}} has no minus signs.
feedback.wrong-x: Count your x strips: {{alg:2x}} needs exactly two.
feedback.wrong-1: Count your small squares: the constant is 3.
feedback.wrong-x2: {{alg:2x + 3}} has no {{alg:x^2}}, so there is no big square.

read-the-tiles.title: Red tiles and zero pairs
read-the-tiles.prompt: What expression do these tiles show? Red tiles are negative. First take off the zero pairs: tap a white tile and a red tile of the same shape. Then type the expression.
read-the-tiles.hint: A white 1 and a red 1 make 0. After taking off the zero pair, count the red small squares that are left.
read-the-tiles.success: Right! {{alg:x^2 + x - 2}}: one big square, one strip and two red small squares.
read-the-tiles.why: Name the terms of {{alg:x^2 + x - 2}}. What is the coefficient of x, and what is the constant?
read-the-tiles.model: The terms are {{alg:x^2}}, {{alg:x}} and {{alg:-2}}. The coefficient of x is 1 (we write x, not 1x), and the constant is −2: the minus sign belongs to the term. A white and a red small square made a zero pair, because 1 + (−1) = 0.

feedback.empty: Type the expression with the keypad.
feedback.syntax: That expression is not finished. Check the last sign.
feedback.not-simplified: Right value, but you can make it simpler: take off the zero pair and add up the numbers.
feedback.white-missed: You forgot the white small square. It cancels one red square: three red and one white leave two red.
feedback.white-as-red: The white small square is +1, not −1. Three red and one white leave two red: −2.
feedback.red-as-white: Red tiles are negative. Three red squares are −3, not +3.
feedback.powers-added: {{alg:x^2}} and {{alg:x}} are different shapes: they are not like terms, so they stay apart. You can't make {{alg:x^3}} from them.
feedback.unlike-added: Only like terms can be put together. {{alg:x^2}}, {{alg:x}} and the numbers are three different kinds.
feedback.sign: Check the signs: which tiles are red?
feedback.wrong-x2: How many big squares are there?
feedback.wrong-x: How many x strips are there?
feedback.wrong-1: Count the small squares again: red ones are negative, and a white and a red make 0.

collect-like-terms.title: Collect like terms
collect-like-terms.prompt: Simplify {{alg:2x^2 + 3x + 1 - x + x^2 - 4}}. Press "Like terms together" to sort the tiles, take off the zero pairs, then type the simplified expression.
collect-like-terms.hint: Big squares go with big squares, strips with strips, small squares with small squares. A red strip cancels one white strip.
collect-like-terms.success: Excellent! {{alg:3x^2 + 2x - 3}}: three big squares, two strips and three red small squares.
collect-like-terms.why: Why can't you add {{alg:3x^2}} and {{alg:2x}} together?
collect-like-terms.model: Because they are not like terms: {{alg:x^2}} and {{alg:x}} are different shapes. You can only count tiles of the same shape. 3 big squares and 2 strips stay as {{alg:3x^2 + 2x}}; writing {{alg:5x^3}} would mix up the shapes and change the value.

feedback.empty: Type the simplified expression with the keypad.
feedback.syntax: That expression is not finished. Check the last sign.
feedback.not-simplified: The value is right, but there are still like terms to put together. Each kind of tile should appear once.
feedback.minus-ignored: The strip in {{alg:-x}} is red: it takes one x away. {{alg:3x - x}} is {{alg:2x}}.
feedback.different-shapes: A red strip and a white square are different shapes: they are not a zero pair. Only the same shape cancels.
feedback.powers-added: {{alg:3x^2}} and {{alg:2x}} are not like terms, so they cannot be added into one term.
feedback.unlike-added: You put together terms that are not alike. Big squares, strips and small squares must stay apart.
feedback.x-plus-x-is-x2: {{alg:x + x}} is {{alg:2x}} (two strips), not {{alg:x^2}} (a big square).
feedback.sign: The sizes are right but a sign is wrong. Which tiles are red?
feedback.wrong-x: Count the strips: three white and one red.
feedback.wrong-1: Count the small squares: one white and four red.

substitute.title: Substitute x = 3
substitute.prompt: What is the value of {{alg:2x + 5}} when {{alg:x = 3}}? Predict first, then flip the tiles and add up what they show.
substitute.hint: Each strip shows 3. There are two strips and five small squares.
substitute.why: Why is {{alg:2x}} equal to 6, and not 23, when {{alg:x = 3}}?
substitute.model: Because 2x means 2 × x, two strips of x. With x = 3 that is 2 × 3 = 6. Writing 23 puts the digits next to each other, which would mean twenty-three, not two threes.

feedback.empty: Type the value with the keypad.
feedback.joined-digits: You wrote 2 next to 3, making 23. But 2x means 2 × x: two strips, each worth 3.
feedback.coefficient-added: You added the 2 instead of multiplying: 2x means 2 × x, not 2 + x.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Flip the tiles and add up exactly what they show.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Flip the tiles and add up exactly what they show.

substitute-negative.title: Substitute a negative number
substitute-negative.prompt: What is the value of {{alg:4 - x^2}} when {{alg:x = -3}}? Predict first, then flip the tiles. The big square is red.
substitute-negative.hint: First square: {{alg:(-3)^2 = 9}}. The big square is red, so take the 9 away from 4.
substitute-negative.why: Why is {{alg:-x^2}} equal to −9, not 9, when {{alg:x = -3}}?
substitute-negative.model: Because the power comes before the minus: −x² means −(x²). First square: (−3)² = 9. Then the minus takes it away, giving −9. Only (−x)², with brackets, would be +9.

feedback.empty: Type the value with the keypad.
feedback.minus-square: You added 9. But the big square is red: −x² means take x² away. First square, then subtract: 4 − 9.
feedback.power-ignored: Don't forget the square: the big square is x², not x. (−3)² = 9.
feedback.sign: Nearly: 4 − 9 is below zero. Which way do you go from 4?
feedback.too-big: Too big. (−3)² is 9, and the big square is red: take 9 away from 4.
feedback.too-small: Too small. (−3)² is 9, and the big square is red: take 9 away from 4.
